title: End of AFO: the Los Angeles trip and Sam Cooke
summary: After Murray cut them off, a trip to a Los Angeles disc-jockey convention turned into a stay, with Sam Cooke giving them a rehearsal studio.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Uh, what, what, what finally, what was the, I shouldn't say the, the death knell, what was the, the end, what was the end of AFO? I mean, what was the?
Well, once that Juggy Murray dried up, uh, our outlet for, to getting our songs played around, we had gone out to, to do a convention for disc jockeys in, in, in Los Angeles.

Now, we were supposed to go out there for two weeks and come back to New Orleans. Right. Unbeknownst to most of us, other than Harold and Melvin, that they figured that's where we should be. Yeah. Now, I didn't know, we didn't know how, uh, John, myself, uh, uh, uh, Chuck Beatty, we were impression we were gonna be two weeks and come back.
What, what they were thinking was, stay, get out there. Stay, set up the business out there. Yeah.

Okay. So, when we got out there and they said, well, look, man, this is where the opportunity is, even though we couldn't work a regular gig out in California because they had strict rules out there that you, for a year, you had to go to the union every week or whatever and, uh, check in that you haven't left town and that after a year you could take a regular job in the club. Oh, okay. You could only do spot jobs. Right. Okay. So, it was getting kinda funny so, uh, we got in touch, uh, with Sam Cook and he said he would open up a little studio for us to rehearse artists that he would bring in and he would give us all fifty dollars a week while we were staying there.

So, I stayed out there as long as I could. When my sister died I came back home. But Harold and Melvin and Tammy and, uh, John Boudreaux stayed out. Uh-huh. And the only one out there now is, uh, John Boudreaux and, uh, Tammy Lynn.
